flashcard_questions.q: What is retribution as an aim of punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: Making the criminal pay for what they have done.

flashcard_questions.q: What is deterrence as an aim of punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: Discouraging crime by showing the consequences of breaking the law.

flashcard_questions.q: What is reformation as an aim of punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: Changing a criminal’s behaviour so they become law-abiding.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Old Testament verse supports retribution in punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: Exodus 21:24 — “an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which parable do Christians use to argue that criminals can be redeemed?
flashcard_questions.a: The Parable of the Lost Son, in Luke 15.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Qur’an 5:39 promise a wrongdoer who repents and reforms?
flashcard_questions.a: That Allah will turn to him in forgiveness.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do critics call prisons “universities of crime”?
flashcard_questions.a: Because offenders can learn new criminal skills there.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Christian charity works inside prisons to support rehabilitation?
What is corporal punishment as a penalty?
flashcard_questions.a: Physical punishment inflicted on the body, such as caning or flogging.

flashcard_questions.q: What is community service as a punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: Unpaid work done in the local community instead of prison.

flashcard_questions.q: When was the ban on the death penalty for murder made permanent in Britain?
What does the principle of utility claim makes an action right?
flashcard_questions.a: That it produces the greatest good for the greatest number of people.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the sanctity of life principle say about taking a life?
flashcard_questions.a: All life is sacred and belongs to God, so no human may take it.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Pope Francis declare about the death penalty in 2018?
flashcard_questions.a: That it is “inadmissible”, and he called for worldwide abolition.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Shari’ah law allow for certain serious offences?
flashcard_questions.a: The death penalty, for offences including murder and apostasy.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (retribution, deterrence, reformation, corporal punishment, community service, utility/sanctity), 4 belief→source (Exodus 21:24, Luke 15, Qur’an 5:39, Shari’ah), 2 denomination→position (Pope Francis 2018, Islamic law), 1 date, 1 named charity, 1 misconception (universities of crime).
